strengths: Well-motivated practical problem: addresses real deployment challenges of state-of-the-art ColPali models (10MB per document, high latency)
Impressive efficiency-quality tradeoffs: achieves 14× speedup and 54× memory reduction compared to Llama-Nemo while maintaining comparable NDCG@5 (62.7 vs 62.9)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: 9 model pairs, 8 hybrid baselines, extensive ablations (Tables 14-17), comparison to cross-encoder reranking
Architecture-agnostic and practical: works with single/multi-vector retrievers, adds only 60-350ms latency, requires no model retraining
Clear presentation and reproducibility: well-written paper with effective visualizations, detailed implementation appendices, promised code release
Robust to design choices: ablations show consistent performance across loss functions (KL, Jensen-Shannon), candidate pool policies, and role assignments
weaknesses: Limited core novelty: combines known techniques (test-time optimization, KL divergence minimization) in straightforward manner; insufficient insight into why this specific combination is effective

Concerning generalization on ViDoRe 1: shows essentially zero improvement (-0.1% average, Table 7), suggesting method may not help when base models already perform well; raises questions about real-world applicability
Requires supervised hyperparameter tuning: demands 10% in-domain development set (not zero-shot); hyperparameters (α, T) appear dataset-dependent, limiting applicability to new domains
Lacks theoretical justification: explicitly empirical focus; no convergence analysis, theoretical guarantees, or principled explanation for when GQR should help; authors acknowledge this limitation
Counterintuitive phenomenon unexplored: text retrievers significantly underperform ColPali (46.8-55.3 vs 60-63 NDCG@5) yet provide helpful guidance; source of complementarity is unexplained
Non-trivial latency overhead: still 2.5× slower than base Colnomic (181ms vs 116ms); 60-350ms overhead may not justify added complexity in latency-sensitive applications
Mixed results and failure modes: scattered negative results (Table 1: -2.4, -0.4) with limited investigation; gains range from +0.3 to +2.8 across settings without systematic characterization

Loss function insensitivity concerning: Table 16 shows different objectives (KL variants, Jensen-Shannon) produce similar results, raising questions about whether method is learning specific to the objective

strengths: Well-motivated practical problem with clear performance-efficiency tradeoff in ColPali models
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with 9 model pairs, 8 baselines, and thorough ablations on ViDoRe 2
Substantial practical efficiency gains (14× faster, 54× less memory) with maintained/improved performance
Architecture-agnostic method applicable to both single and multi-vector retrievers
Clear presentation with effective visualizations and promised code release for reproducibility
weaknesses: Limited novelty: straightforward application of existing test-time query refinement (Sung et al. 2023, Gangi Reddy et al. 2025) with bi-encoder instead of cross-encoder—incremental contribution inadequately distinguished from prior work

No theoretical justification for design choices: Why KL(p_avg||p1)? Table 16 shows similar results for JS and KL(p2||p1), undermining the specific divergence choice; no convergence analysis or optimality guarantees
Serious generalization concern: ViDoRe 1 shows -0.1% average gain vs. +3.9% on ViDoRe 2, suggesting potential overfitting; paper dismisses via 'saturation' rather than investigating root causes
Requires hyperparameter tuning (T, α) on in-domain development set per-subset, limiting zero-shot applicability and practical deployment flexibility compared to parameter-free baselines

Insufficient analysis of when/why GQR works: No intuition for why weaker text retrievers guide vision models; no error analysis, query type categorization, or visualization of refined representations; inconsistent gains across subsets unexplained
Inconsistent implementation details: Adam optimizer used in practice but gradient descent described in main method; critical implementation choices relegated to footnotes
Candidate pool design not well justified: Table 15 shows inconsistent effects of union vs. top-K policy, weakening design choices
Modest gains in key settings with no statistical significance testing: +0.3-1.2 NDCG@5 for strongest baseline (Llama-Nemo) without error bars or confidence intervals
Inference cost non-negligible: 50-170% latency overhead for Colnomic models (60-194ms on 116ms baseline) inadequately discussed for latency-constrained applications
Limited sensitivity analysis: Only K=10 tested; effects of iterations T and learning rate α unexplored; no ablation on equal weighting assumption in consensus distribution

strengths: Addresses important practical problem: achieving SOTA retrieval performance with significant efficiency constraints (14× speedup, 54× memory reduction)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: two benchmarks, 9 model pairs, proper baselines (ranking/score-level aggregation, weighted variants, rerankers), and extensive ablations
Strong empirical results on primary benchmark: consistent +3.9% average NDCG@5 gain on ViDoRe 2 with compelling Pareto improvements

Well-designed approach: representation-level hybrid method is elegant, operating between coarse-grained ranking/score fusion and full representation alignment, architecture-agnostic across single/multi-vector retrievers

Thorough experimental rigor: Tables 14-17 systematically ablate design choices (candidate pool, loss functions, role swapping), proper train/dev/test splits, latency and memory measurements on dedicated hardware
Clear presentation with effective visualizations, implementation details provided, code release promised, reproducible on public benchmarks
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: core technique (KL divergence-based distribution alignment for test-time query refinement) applies existing methods to new domain; test-time refinement with feedback previously explored (Yu et al. 2021; Sung et al. 2023)

Weak generalization across benchmarks: ViDoRe 1 shows essentially no improvements (mostly ±0.0-0.1% per Table 5); paper attributes to saturation but this significantly limits evidence for broad applicability

Requires in-domain hyperparameter tuning: GQR needs T and α tuned on development set (10% per subset), violating zero-shot applicability and adding deployment complexity compared to parameter-free methods

Incomplete latency-accuracy analysis: adds 60-350ms per query overhead; paper doesn't thoroughly analyze when this cost is justified vs. using larger base models, or explore sensitivity to suboptimal hyperparameters
Asymmetric primary/complementary role design lacks principled selection strategy; Table 17 explores swapping but doesn't provide guidance for new scenarios
Candidate pool limitation: method restricted to union of top-K from both retrievers, inherently limiting recall for documents outside initial rankings
Limited reranker comparison: only one reranker baseline (MonoQwen2-VL); reranking is standard production approach deserving more comprehensive comparison across models and K values
Minimal theoretical justification: purely empirical work without analysis of why this distribution alignment succeeds or what properties of ColPali enable effective refinement
Missing ablations: unclear how much gain comes from union of top-K vs. iterative refinement; limited error analysis on which query types benefit most/least

strengths: Well-motivated problem with clear practical impact: demonstrates 14× latency reduction and 54× memory savings compared to LLAMA-NEMORETRIEVER while achieving competitive performance
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: 3 established benchmarks (ViDoRe 1/2/3), 9 model pairs, both tuned and zero-shot settings, thorough ablations on hyperparameters and design choices
Consistent improvements across all evaluated hybrid methods: GQR achieves 3.9% average gain on ViDoRe 2, outperforming tuned score aggregation (3.4%) and ranking fusion methods
Architecture-agnostic approach applicable to both single- and multi-vector embeddings, with clear algorithmic description and promised code release for reproducibility
Insightful analysis: hyperparameter investigation reveals interpretable tradeoffs, per-query dynamics demonstrate distinctness from score aggregation, latency breakdown quantifies optimization costs
Practical Pareto frontier improvements: clearly demonstrates efficiency-performance tradeoffs across multiple models with detailed latency/memory measurements
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: core contribution is adapting existing test-time query optimization (Yu et al. 2021, Sung et al. 2023) by replacing cross-encoder with bi-encoder guidance—incremental rather than transformative

Modest empirical gains on strongest baselines: LLAMA-NEMORETRIEVER (63.0→65.2, +2.2), COLNOMIC-7B (60.3→63.1, +2.8); improvements diminish when compared to tuned baselines (3.9% vs 3.4% for tuned Score Aggregation)

Lacks theoretical justification: unclear why KL(p_avg||p₁) is optimal when Table 18 shows Jensen-Shannon and KL(p₂||p₁) perform 'similarly well'; consensus distribution (simple 0.5 weighting) appears arbitrary without learned alternatives tested

Hyperparameter sensitivity without strong zero-shot generalization: 2 hyperparameters (α, T) with high variance (Figure 4); zero-shot ViDoRe 3 results only marginally exceed tuned baselines (2.89% vs 2.66%), suggesting limited domain generalization

Evaluation limited to visual document retrieval: no evidence of applicability to dense retrieval, QA, e-commerce or other domains; ViDoRe 1 saturated (90+ on many subsets) limiting utility; zero-shot uses ViDoRe 2 hyperparameters

Insufficient analysis of failure modes and complementary retriever quality impact: unexplained degradation in some model pairs (e.g., +0.7 gain on ESG Human for Colnomic+Qwen3); no systematic investigation of when/why GQR works
Non-trivial latency overhead masked by framing: 50-100ms optimization cost represents 56% latency increase for Colnomic (115.98→181.21ms), potentially problematic for latency-sensitive applications

Experimental design inconsistencies: text models use Docling OCR (variable quality) on ViDoRe 1/2 while vision models use images; ViDoRe 3 uses markdown for text models but images for vision models—different content modalities confound comparisons
Missing statistical significance testing and incomplete baseline comparisons: marginal improvements over tuned Score Aggregation with comparable standard deviations lack statistical validation
Insufficient intuition for practitioners: unclear guidance on when to apply GQR, how complementary retriever quality affects performance, or why certain model pairs underperform

strengths: Clear problem motivation addressing real deployment challenges (efficiency vs. quality tradeoff in multimodal retrieval)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across three benchmarks with systematic ablations and design choice justifications
Practical impact demonstrated (14× speedup, 54× memory reduction) while maintaining competitive performance
Thorough empirical analysis including hyperparameter sweeps, per-query dynamics, reranking comparisons, and latency breakdowns
Good reproducibility effort with implementation details and promise of code release
weaknesses: Limited novelty: test-time query optimization via pseudo-relevance feedback is well-established (Yu et al. 2021, Sung et al. 2023); the main contribution—using a lightweight bi-encoder instead of a cross-encoder—is engineering-focused rather than methodologically novel

Modest and inconsistent improvements: 3.9% average on ViDoRe 2 (range 1.5%-8.7% across subsets), negligible gains on ViDoRe 1, with many individual cases showing ≤1% improvement that lack statistical significance testing

Weak theoretical justification: Table 18 shows different loss functions (JS, KL consensus, KL target) perform nearly identically, undermining the specific contribution; why consensus averaging at 0.5/0.5 is superior to alternatives is not principled
Single-task and single-domain evaluation: only visual document retrieval tested; generalizability to other multimodal tasks (image-text, video retrieval) or modality combinations is unclear

High hyperparameter sensitivity: Section 4.1 reveals significant variance across learning rate (α) and optimization steps (T) combinations, contradicting claims of simplicity; Tables 20-21 show no single configuration generalizes across model pairs

Incomplete experimental rigor: no statistical significance testing with error bars or confidence intervals; claimed 'zero-shot' on ViDoRe 3 actually uses hyperparameters tuned on ViDoRe 2 (should be called transfer, not zero-shot)

Arbitrary design choices lacking ablation: why union of candidate pools over intersection (Table 17 shows inconsistent effects); why softmax over C(q) not full index; why Adam over SGD (only 'preliminary experiments' mentioned); why fixed 0.5/0.5 consensus weight

Limited error analysis and failure modes: no characterization of when/why GQR helps or hurts; when do weak complementary signals degrade primary performance; missing query/document-level analysis of success/failure patterns

strengths: Exceptional experimental rigor: comprehensive evaluation across 3 benchmarks, 9 model pairs, multiple baselines, ablations, and both tuned/zero-shot settings with reproducible implementation
Well-motivated practical problem: addresses real deployment constraints (14× latency reduction, 54× memory reduction) with clear Pareto frontier improvements
Consistent empirical gains: achieves near SOTA performance with modest overhead across diverse model pairs and benchmark subsets (low variance σ=1.9)
Clean architectural design: representation-level fusion allows adaptive, non-linear query refinement constrained by primary model geometry—elegant middle ground between ranking and score fusion
Strong reproducibility: released code, detailed hyperparameter tables, ablations on design choices (loss functions, candidate pools, role assignments), clear algorithmic description
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: applies established test-time query optimization (Yu et al. 2021, Sung et al. 2023) to hybrid retrieval by substituting lightweight bi-encoder for cross-encoder—incremental contribution
Narrow evaluation scope: exclusively visual document retrieval; generalization to dense passage retrieval, image search, or other tasks remains unexplored and unclear

Insufficient mechanistic analysis: paper doesn't explain why text guidance helps vision models, which complementary retrievers work best, or query-level factors driving success; only 6 per-query examples in Figure 8

Hyperparameter sensitivity without principled selection: Figure 4 shows significant α-T interaction effects; zero-shot config (10^-4, T=50) appears arbitrary; practical deployment requires per-task tuning

Candidate pool constraints: method refines only within union of top-K documents; Table 17 shows mixed effects of switching to primary-only; no gains from second index search (Table 16) suggests limited recall potential

Occasional failure modes unexplained: Table 1 shows degradations for weak complementary retrievers (Qwen3 pairs); strongest baseline (Llama-Nemo) shows smallest gains; ViDoRe 1 saturation limits interpretability
